brief: Goldman Prime Services' weekly rundown: US equities bifurcated this week, AI-linked exposures selling off (Semis -8% Friday, NDX down ~7% in October) while non-AI names (IBM, AAPL, SPOT, V/MA, EBAY, LYV) and defensives (Healthcare, Biotech, Defense Spending) outperformed. Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in four weeks, driven by short covers in Macro Products, but Info Tech remains heavily net sold month-to-date and Mag 7 names were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, so the desk reads little recovery in risk appetite. Financials saw the fastest de-grossing in over six months. A sharp vol crush reversed Friday as flows caught up to the bear thesis: desks bought downside in index and semis, S&P broke its medium-term CTA momentum threshold, and a further break would flip GS systematic momentum negative, halting CTA buying. Market breadth stayed healthy despite the tech-led drop. Ahead of midterms (Kalshi: 65% odds of a Democratic sweep), GS outlines five affordability-linked equity baskets spanning ACA subsidies, drug pricing, power-cost allocation, government spending, and corporate tax exposure.
